scams.name: The Philae Temple Boat Gouge
scams.tldr: You arrive at the Shellal motorboat dock south of Aswan ready to cross to Philae Island for the Temple of Isis.
scams.description: You arrive at the Shellal motorboat dock south of Aswan ready to cross to Philae Island for the Temple of Isis. The official rate posted on a sign beside the dock is 10 Egyptian pounds. The first boatman you approach laughs at the sign. "That price is old, my friend — five hundred pounds, round trip, with one hour wait. You want to see the temple, you take my boat."
scams.avoidance: Negotiate firmly — a fair round-trip price is 150-200 EGP per boat (not per person) with a one-hour wait. Clarify all terms before boarding: round trip, total price, wait time on the island, and no extras. Visit early morning when fewer tourists mean less demand and easier negotiation. Book the boat through your hotel or a tour package that includes Philae transport at a fixed price. Bring your own water and snacks — the cafe on Philae Island charges extreme markup as the only vendor.
scams.location: Motorboat dock at Shellal, south of Aswan (access point for Philae Temple)

scams.name: The Airport Taxi Ambush
scams.tldr: You walk out of Aswan International Arrivals into dry desert heat and a wall of taxi drivers descends.
scams.description: You walk out of Aswan International Arrivals into dry desert heat and a wall of taxi drivers descends. The first one grabs your suitcase handle before you've made eye contact. "Taxi? Five hundred pounds to your hotel, my friend." Five hundred pounds is roughly $30 — for a 25-kilometer ride that should run about 100 to 150 EGP.
scams.avoidance: Arrange airport pickup through your hotel before arriving — most Aswan hotels offer this at fair rates. If negotiating at the stand, walk away from the first cluster of drivers and look for solo taxis further down. Know the approximate distance: Aswan airport to central Aswan is about 25 km, fair price 100-150 EGP. Share a taxi with other arriving tourists to split the inflated cost. Have your hotel's phone number ready to call for pickup if taxi prices are unreasonable.

scams.name: The Felucca Bait-and-Pressure
scams.tldr: You're walking the Aswan Corniche near the Ferial Garden at sunset, the lateen sails of a dozen feluccas catching the last orange light.
scams.description: You're walking the Aswan Corniche near the Ferial Garden at sunset, the lateen sails of a dozen feluccas catching the last orange light. A captain steps over and offers a one-hour sail for 100 EGP — fair, beautiful timing. You agree, step aboard, and he pushes off into the soft current of the Nile.
scams.avoidance: Set expectations clearly: 'One-hour sail only, no stops, no shopping, agreed price of [X] EGP.' A fair price for a one-hour felucca sail in Aswan is 150–250 EGP. Ask your hotel to recommend a trusted felucca captain they regularly work with. Sail in the late afternoon when winds are reliable and the experience is genuinely beautiful. Pay half upfront and half when you return to the dock at the agreed time.
scams.location: Along the Aswan Corniche near the Ferial Garden and Elephantine Island ferry

scams.name: The Spice Souk Switch
scams.tldr: You wander into the Aswan souk on Sharia as-Souq, the air heavy with cardamom and saffron.
scams.description: You wander into the Aswan souk on Sharia as-Souq, the air heavy with cardamom and saffron. A spice seller calls you in, smiles, hands you a small vial. "Smell — pure jasmine oil, from the Fayoum oasis." The fragrance is rich and unmistakable. You ask the price; he names a number that sounds reasonable for the small bottle in his hand.
scams.avoidance: Insist on watching the entire pouring process from the exact bottle you smelled. Smell the sealed final product before handing over any money. Agree on the price and specific items BEFORE any measuring begins. Politely refuse all free extras — say 'only what I asked for, nothing more.' Compare prices at multiple stalls in the souk before buying — the Aswan souk has dozens of spice vendors.
scams.location: Spice stalls in the Aswan Souk (Sharia as-Souq)

scams.name: The Nubian Village Tourist Trap
scams.tldr: Your tour guide brings you across the Nile to Gharb Soheil, advertised as a traditional Nubian village.
scams.description: Your tour guide brings you across the Nile to Gharb Soheil, advertised as a traditional Nubian village. The houses are painted in striking blues and yellows, kids run up smiling, and a man holds up a crocodile in a painted basin offering a photo opportunity. The first impression is genuine.
scams.avoidance: Visit Nubian villages independently by hiring a motorboat from the Corniche rather than through a tour. Ask prices before accepting any service, activity, or hospitality. Bargain respectfully — starting at 30-40 percent of the first quoted price is normal. Carry small bills so you can pay exact amounts without change disputes. Walk past the main tourist strip to find more authentic Nubian experiences further from the dock.
scams.location: Nubian villages on the West Bank, particularly Gharb Soheil

scams.name: The Taxi Fare Bait-and-Switch
scams.tldr: You flag a taxi outside the Nubian Museum heading for the Aswan train station to catch the night sleeper to Cairo.
scams.description: You flag a taxi outside the Nubian Museum heading for the Aswan train station to catch the night sleeper to Cairo. You agree on 25 EGP — a fair fare for the short ride. The driver nods, smiles, gestures for your luggage, and starts driving.
scams.avoidance: State the price clearly: 'Twenty-five Egyptian pounds. Khamsa w-ishreen gineih Masri.' Get verbal confirmation. Write the agreed price on your phone and show it to the driver before departing. Keep your luggage with you in the back seat rather than in the trunk when possible. Ask your hotel for typical taxi fares between major sites so you know fair prices. If a driver tries to hold your luggage hostage, tell him you'll call the Tourist Police.
scams.location: Between major sites: Nubian Museum, train station, Old Cataract Hotel, and Unfinished Obelisk
